fact: World Bank's Stephane Guimbert says Takaful and Karama pays through digital Meeza cards, which cut leakages and enhanced transparency.

fact: The World Bank says it continues to support Egypt's Takaful and Karama programme by building the management information system.
system: Takaful and Karama management information system

fact: The World Bank says 100 percent of Takaful and Karama beneficiaries are paid through electronic means, via Meeza debit cards, as of December 2023.

Egypt's unified government services card system is being rolled out in phases, with phase one in Port Said, phase two in Ismailia and Luxor and phase three planned for the remaining governorates, as reported to the Prime Minister.

The Ministry of Social Solidarity said Takaful and Karama beneficiaries, 4.7 million families, receive June 2026 payments electronically through bank ATMs, Nasser Social Bank branches, Fawry outlets and the programme's Meeza cards.

Takaful and Karama pensions are sent monthly to beneficiaries' mobile wallets once a social unit enters the request on the system and links the pension to the wallet, per the Ministry of Social Solidarity as reported.

Takaful and Karama, the conditional cash transfer programme, runs on an integrated software system that verifies applicants' socio-economic data, per the Ministry of Social Solidarity's Raafat Shafik.
